w: London, 21 June 1970

According to Yogiji Maharaj's fixed programme, Swamishri was to depart from here for India on 22 June 1970. But later, because of difficulties with the flight and the route, that programme was cancelled. The youths and devotees here had also been pressing him very strongly. Swamishri stayed on to give everyone more happiness.

Enduring great hardship, the youths and devotees were benefiting from serving and associating with Swamishri. The festivals too were divine. Swamishri's birthday celebration and the murti pratishtha (image consecration) festival of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj were wonderful, and the public satsang assemblies also made a good impression. Among the Indian population of England too, this special visit of a sadhu brought a unique enthusiasm. Hindu pride was awakened.

Dilip Vedalankar, a preacher of the Hindu dharma, was going to America. When he came longing for Swamishri's blessings, Swamishri said, "You must spread three things. First, give the message of Bhagwan Swaminarayan; second, explain to everyone that they should give up addictions; and third, speak about the spirit of unity. We Hindus are all one, and we should live in harmony."
Sadhu Ishwarcharandas

In the evening assembly, the Kishores presented a program, Leicester Satsang - Past, Present and Future. The special program was interwoven with dialogues, skits, a slide show and speeches that traced the establishment of the mandir in 1977 to the fostering of Satsang activities by Swamishri. The program was crowned with Swamishri's blessings.

Swamishri celebrated Rath Yatra festival by guiding a chariot of Thakorji through a remote control contraption. In the evening session of the shibir, Viveksagar Swami explained the history and significance of Rath Yatra festival and Swamishri blessed the assembly.

Children's Day This morning, 2,000 local children from twelve regions of Valsad district had assembled for the special Children's Day assembly. The program featured an impressive march-dance, a speech and a local welcome dance by children. In conclusion, Swamishri addressed the assembly.

ph: Swamishri prays prior to blessing the assembly

w: While Swamishri was taking his medicine he asked someone, “Would you like to have this?” The person replied, “Give me medicine that will cure me from the disease of the cycles of birth and death. And bless me that I am able to drink it no matter how bitter it is.” Swamishri instantly replied, “You have been given the medicine of listening to spiritual discourses ( katha ) and engaging in bhajan and kirtan. These are the medicines you have to take because they will help you to remain stable amid praise and insult, and joy and misery.”

A student expressed, “I love reading the Vachanamrut, but don’t feel like reading my school textbooks at all.” Swamishri encouraged him, “You must read both the Vachanamrut and your textbooks. By studying at school you’ll be able to make a career in life and by reading the Vachanamrut you will get spiritual knowledge. This will enable you to tide over joy and misery in life. You must learn to balance your life.”

ds.t: Medicine for the disease of worldly life
w: After his morning puja, Pramukh Swami Maharaj was taking his medicine as part of his daily routine when Dharmapurush Swami was standing in front. Seeing his special way of laughing, Swamishri's attention went to him. Swamishri said to him, "Do you want some medicine?"
"If there is medicine that cures the disease of worldly life, please give it, and bless us that however bitter it tastes, we can still drink it."

Swamishri immediately said, "The medicine has already been given, hasn't it: spiritual discourses, bhajans and kirtans. These are all medicines to be taken, so that one can cope with honour and insult, happiness and sorrow, and nothing troubles one."

A student living in the Surat hostel came today for the darshan of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Making his complaint, the student said, "I feel like reading the Vachanamrut, but I do not feel like reading my study books at all."

Swamishri immediately said, "You have to read the Vachanamrut and you also have to read your study books. If we study, our life is made, and if we read the Vachanamrut, we gain knowledge. Then there is no trouble in happiness or sorrow. Learn to keep a balance between the two."

ds.t: Hold Maharaj in your heart and worship
w: After lunch, during a conversation on the occasion, Pramukh Swami Maharaj spoke of Shastriji Maharaj's principle: "Shastriji Maharaj had only one principle: there is nothing to be gained by fighting with anyone. If we fight, the other side will dig up everything under the sun. If not one thing then another, and if not that then a third; they will keep digging. Rather than that, if we are in the right, hold Maharaj in your heart and do bhajan. Go everywhere for darshan. Do not criticise anyone. Even when people wrote against him, he did not reply. The basic foundation is to remain firm in what is true and to do only what is right. Even if we fail while doing what is right, it does not matter."

The social worker Fakirchand Rustagi said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "Some instruction, please...."
Swamishri said, "Have darshan of God and remember him."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj met Bharatsinh Solanki, Minister of State for Power in the Government of India. Swamishri remembered the services of his father, Madhavsinh Solanki.

Bharatsinh Solanki said, "On the way, I told all the IAS officers who are with me about your glory, how this organisation is managed and with what feeling the work is done here. In Delhi, it has become such that everyone who comes feels that they simply must go to Akshardham. People come and stay at my place too for this very reason. They phone us and say, 'We want to see Akshardham, so we will stay at your place.' And I too make arrangements for everyone." Having said this, he said, "I have two requests. First, the rain has not yet come, and second, please pray that the work on the Narmada canal in Gujarat is completed. Without someone like you, no one can do great work." Finally he said, "Your management is worth understanding and putting into practice."
Swamishri said, "God does everything."

During Mahant Swami Maharaj's walk, a reading from the book "Yogi Vani" began. In it came the talk: "One has to serve everyone, see everyone as faultless and not find fault with anyone; then Maharaj will let one into Akshardham."
Swamishri pointed out the key point: "Everyone's; then one can go to Akshardham. That is the passport."
